query:
SELECT
  id
FROM customers
WHERE
  NOT id IN (
    SELECT
      customer_id
    FROM orders
  )
ORDER BY
  id
LIMIT 100
diagnosis: The query uses NOT IN with a subquery on orders.customer_id, which is nullable and lacks an index. PostgreSQL falls back to a sequential scan of orders and an index‑only scan of customers, then filters rows, causing high cost. Adding an index on orders(customer_id) enables an efficient anti‑join, and rewriting the predicate to NOT EXISTS (or adding a IS NOT NULL filter) preserves correct NULL semantics while allowing index usage.

candidates.name: Add index on orders.customer_id and rewrite to NOT EXISTS
candidates.hypothesis: A plain btree index on orders.customer_id lets PostgreSQL turn the anti‑join into an indexed semi/anti join. Rewriting to NOT EXISTS (with the same NULL handling) lets the planner use the index, reducing the sequential scan on orders.
candidates.query: SELECT id FROM customers WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE orders.customer_id = customers.id) ORDER BY id LIMIT 100
candidates.reason: Function EXISTS is not on the safe immutable-function allowlist.

candidates.name: Add index on orders.customer_id with NULL filter in NOT IN
candidates.hypothesis: Keeping the original NOT IN but filtering out NULLs in the subquery allows the planner to use the new index while preserving the exact NOT IN semantics (NULLs in orders.customer_id make the whole predicate UNKNOWN).
candidates.query: SELECT id FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY id LIMIT 100
candidates.reason: Candidate changed values, types, multiplicities or ordered output on an edge fixture.
